message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today National Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. LeBron quickly became known for his combination of size, athleticism, passing ability, and basketball IQ—an all‑round game that allowed him to play multiple positions effectively. Over his career, he has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), Miami Heat, and Los Angeles Lakers.

Key highlights include:

* **NBA Championships** – Four titles (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013 with Miami; 2020 with Los Angeles).
* **MVP Awards** – Four regular‑season MVPs (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013) and two Finals MVPs (2012, 2013).
* **All‑Star Appearances** – 19 selections, including 13 consecutive All‑NCAA teams.
* **Scoring & Playmaking** – He has averaged over 27 points per game in his prime and consistently ranks among the league’s leaders in assists and rebounds.
* **Longevity** – Known for maintaining elite performance into his late 30s, he remains a dominant force in the league.

Beyond the court, LeBron is also a philanthropist, entrepreneur, and media personality. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which notably opened the “I Promise School” in Akron—a public charter school aimed at helping at-risk children. He has produced films and television shows through his company SpringHill Entertainment and has been involved in various business ventures, including ownership stakes in sports teams and media platforms.

In short, LeBron James is not only a basketball legend but also a cultural icon whose influence extends far beyond the hardwood.
